title: Reason about migrating a stale account from the client side
prompt: A user has an account that was created before our most recent upgrade, so its stored schema version is behind the program's current version. They are calling `Increment` and the transaction fails. Explain what is happening and what has to change on chain for their call to succeed — then make the program handle this situation itself so the user does not have to send a separate migration transaction. Keep the program building and the migration history consistent.
expectation: A stale account fails the current-only loaders with `MigrationRequired`. The program-owned fix is to call `MigrateAccount::invoke::<T>()` inside the instruction that touches the account (which the fixture already does) or to rely on the reserved `Migrate` route wired by `#[discriminator(entrypoint)]`. The agent should recognize the existing `MigrateAccount` call and the reserved route rather than inventing a new instruction or asking the client to send extra transactions.

checks.why: The symptom must be traced to the stale-account version gate.
Program-owned migration is the documented mechanism for an instruction that touches a stale account.
The reserved framework route is the out-of-band path and should be named.
Inventing a bespoke migration instruction duplicates the reserved route.
Any schema change must leave the migration history consistent.
